Your AI Copilot Is Already Inside SAP Datasphere... Are You Using It? 

Here's something a lot of SAP Datasphere users don't realize: Joule, SAP's generative AI copilot, is embedded directly in Datasphere. Not in a separate tool, but directly in the platform you're already working on every day. 

Many data professionals associate Joule with SAP S/4HANA or SAP Analytics Cloud. And while Joule is also present in those products, its integration with Datasphere is one of the more quietly powerful capabilities in your SAP Business Data Cloud environment. 

What is Joule for Datasphere? 

Joule in Datasphere supports three categories of tasks: informational, navigational, and transactional. Together, they cover a meaningful slice of the day-to-day work data professionals do inside the tool. 

Informational: Ask Joule how to use a specific Datasphere feature and get an answer grounded in product documentation without leaving the platform to hunt through help pages or community posts. You can also query Joule for instance-specific information about your own Datasphere environment. 

Navigational: Joule can guide you through tasks and help you move around the platform more efficiently. For newer team members or occasional users, this can significantly reduce the learning curve. 

Transactional: This is where it gets genuinely interesting for data engineers and modelers. Joule supports AI-assisted SQL generation directly in the SQL View Builder. This means that you can describe what you want in natural language, and Joule generates the SQL. Whether you're creating a new SQL view from scratch or modifying an existing one, this capability can meaningfully cut down the time spent writing and debugging queries. 

Joule also supports AI-assisted semantic generation, automatically recognizing and assigning semantic types for ingested non-SAP data, which is typically a manual and time-consuming preparation step. 

Why it Matters to Data Professionals 

The honest reality of working with data at scale is that a significant portion of the time goes into maintenance tasks: figuring out the right syntax, navigating documentation, writing boilerplate SQL, manually classifying fields. These tasks take valuable time out of your day and eat into time that could be spent making strategic business decisions. Joule helps give you that time back! It doesn't replace your judgment, but rather it takes on the mechanical parts, so you can focus on the work that actually requires your expertise. 

For data modelers, the SQL generation capability alone is worth exploring. For enterprise architects managing complex environments with many users at different skill levels, the informational and navigational capabilities help teams work more independently and consistently. 

Why You May Have Missed It 

Joule in Datasphere needs to be activated at the tenant level and requires users to have the appropriate privilege assigned. It doesn't switch on automatically. That setup step means a lot of teams have Joule available but haven't enabled it, or have enabled it without communicating it to the people who would benefit most. 

If you're a Datasphere administrator reading this, it's worth checking whether Joule is active in your environment and whether your modelers and data engineers know it's there.

Give it a try in your own environment and see how much of your workflow it can simplify.

entry.title: Track Your Private Cloud Journey: New Adoption Milestones powered by SAP EarlyWatch Alert
entry.content:
We are excited to announce a new capability for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition customers: adoption milestone tracking, powered by SAP EarlyWatch Alert data and available in the Customer Insights Dashboard (CID) on SAP for Me.

If you are already familiar with the onboarding milestones for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP), this is the Private Cloud counterpart you have been waiting for. And it goes even further: in addition to tracking implementation progress, the new milestones include built-in adoption risk monitoring that continuously watches for early signs of stalled implementations or declining system usage.

 

Why This Matters

Moving to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition is one of the most significant transformations a business can undertake. The journey from contract signature to a fully operational, value-generating system can span months, sometimes even years, of provisioning, configuration, testing and go-live activities.

Yet for much of that journey, the signals that indicate whether a customer is progressing as expected, or beginning to stall, have been difficult to surface systematically. Data was fragmented across tools, inputs were manual, and adoption risk was often identified too late for meaningful intervention.

The question we set out to answer: How can we generate data-driven insights on adoption journeys, early enough to make a real difference?

 

What SAP EarlyWatch Alert Brings to the Table

SAP EarlyWatch Alert has been a trusted companion for SAP customers for decades, indicating system health, performance, and configuration. With this new release, SAP EarlyWatch Alert further expands its scope beyond system diagnostics into adoption intelligence. Here is what makes this approach unique:

  • Zero configuration. SAP EarlyWatch Alert already collects weekly telemetry data from every connected system: active users, transport activity, transaction usage, and more. No additional setup is required from the customer.
  • Fully automated. Milestones are automatically recalculated twice per week across all connected S/4HANA Private Cloud landscapes.
  • Proactive risk detection. The dashboard does not just track forward progress. It also continuously monitors signs of stalled adoption and user decline after go-live.
  • Integrated experience. Milestone data appears in the Onboarding tab of the Customer Insights Dashboard in SAP for Me, right alongside Public Cloud and IBP milestones.

The SAP EarlyWatch Alert Apps as tools for proactive alerting and diagnostics can be accessed via SAP for Me: https://me.sap.com/servicessupport/diagnostics

 

The Six Adoption Milestones

Each SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition system landscape is tracked through six milestones that map to the key phases of a new cloud ERP implementation or transformation approach. Milestones are evaluated per system track, which is the logical grouping of a customer's Development (DEV), Test (TEST), and Production (PROD) systems linked by a common SAP Transport Management System route.

M1: Landscape Initialized

Your S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition system is live and connected to SAP. Your implementation journey has now begun.

This milestone is triggered when the first EarlyWatch Alert data is received from any non-production system in the track. It marks the moment the landscape becomes visible to SAP. No thresholds and no configuration are needed. The mere presence of this data confirms that provisioning is complete and the system is connected.

M2: Realize Phase Active

Your team has started configuring the system for your business needs. Build and testing activities are now underway.

Detected through usage of transaction SPRO (the SAP Customizing Implementation Guide) on a DEV or TEST system. SPRO is the central entry point for system configuration, so its usage is a reliable signal that the implementation team has begun tailoring the system to the customer's business processes.

M3: Pre-Cutover Preparation

Access roles and authorization profiles are being set up. Go-live preparation is underway.

Detected through usage of transaction PFCG (Role Maintenance) on a non-production system. Setting up authorization roles and user profiles is a critical pre-go-live activity.

M4: Cutover Initiated

Your team has initiated the cutover; configuration is being transported to your production system. Go-live is imminent.

Triggered when a significant transport wave is detected on the production system: at least 1,000 Workbench and Customizing transport objects imported in a single week. This threshold distinguishes genuine cutover deployments from routine maintenance imports and provides a high-confidence signal that go-live preparation is in its final stage.

M5: Go-Live Detected

A significant jump in active users on your production system confirms go-live. Your system is now in productive use.

SAP EarlyWatch Alert tracks weekly active user counts on the production system. When a significant and sustained spike in users is detected, the system is considered live. The detection automatically adapts to the size of each customer's landscape, so it works equally well for small and large deployments. It also accounts for special cases like system conversions and filters out technical-only activity to avoid false positives.

M6: Steady Usage State

Your system is in stable productive use with an active user base and regular updates. The status is reviewed continuously and may change.

Unlike M1 through M5, which are set once and remain, M6 is a living indicator. It is re-evaluated every week and can change between "Reached" (healthy) and "At Risk" based on two independent checks.

M6-1: Transport Activity Check. Were any transports imported into any system in the track within the last six months? If not, the system may no longer be actively maintained. This check runs independently of go-live status, so it can flag adoption stalls even before a customer has gone live.

M6-2: User Decline Detection. After go-live, the system continuously monitors whether the number of active users on the production system is declining significantly. A sustained drop in usage serves as an early signal for customer success teams to reach out and offer support.

Remark: Some milestones can be calculated based on the availability of connected Private Cloud systems.

 

Where to Find It

The milestone data is available in the Customer Insights Dashboard (CID) on SAP for Me, in the Onboarding tab: https://me.sap.com/reporting/customerinsightsdashboard/onboarding

If you are already using the Onboarding view for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition or SAP IBP, you will find the Private Cloud milestones right alongside them. Same dashboard, same experience, no additional setup:

When M6 turns red, it provides a specific, actionable signal: either maintenance activity has stopped or the productive user base is declining. Both are leading indicators of adoption challenges, and both are surfaced early enough for proactive engagement.

 

Conclusion

Adoption milestone tracking for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition transforms EarlyWatch Alert data, collected every week from every connected system, into structured, actionable adoption intelligence. By automatically identifying where each customer stands in their cloud journey and flagging early signs of risk, it enables the kind of proactive, data-driven engagement that complex cloud transformations demand.

Read more about how this helps you get the most out of your SAP investment: Proactive by Design: Introducing Adoption Milestone Tracking for S/4HANA Private Cloud - SAP Community

The data is already there. Now, it tells a story.

entry.title: SAP CPQ : The Future of Sales Quoting Is Here: Meet SAP's Joule Quoting Assistant
entry.content:
How AI is transforming one of sales' most time-consuming processes

Every sales rep knows the pain. A customer sends over an email — or a ten-page PDF — and suddenly you're spending the better part of your afternoon manually parsing the request, matching products, checking pricing rules, and assembling a proposal document. It's repetitive, error-prone, and it gets in the way of actual selling.

 

SAP's Joule Quoting Assistant is designed to change that entirely.

What Is the Joule Quoting Assistant?

The Joule Quoting Assistant is an AI-powered Joule Assistant — part of SAP's broader agentic AI portfolio — built specifically for the quote-to-order cycle. Its core mission: transform unstructured customer requests into accurate, compliant quotes with AI-guided selling across the entire SAP CPQ (Configure, Price, Quote) flow. Source

It sits at the intersection of SAP CPQ, SAP Sales Cloud, and SAP S/4HANA, orchestrating specialized AI agents behind the scenes to handle tasks that would otherwise fall to the sales rep or a back-office support team.

From Inbox to Quote: What It Actually Does

Here's where the Quoting Assistant gets practical. Given an unstructured customer inquiry — whether it arrives as an email, a request for quotation (RFQ), or a PDF — the assistant can:

  • Convert the raw request into a structured CPQ quote draft, extracting relevant intent and mapping it to your product catalog and pricing rules.
  • Recommend compliant product configurations based on what the customer described in natural language — no need to manually navigate complex configurators.
  • Surface real-time upsell, add-on, and cross-sell options guided by historical deal data and pricing policies.
  • Assemble proposal documents and draft customer-facing emails, ready for the rep to review and send.
  • Route multi-step requests to the right specialized agents automatically, without manual handoffs.
  • Enforce pricing and discount policies — every quote stays within guardrails, reducing approvals overhead and compliance risk. Source

Why This Matters for your Sales Teams

The shift from manual quoting to AI-guided quoting isn't just about speed — it changes the quality and consistency of the entire sales conversation.

Faster time to first draft. Instead of spending hours building a quote from scratch, reps get an intelligent draft that's already shaped by the customer's actual request. That frees them up to focus on relationship management and deal strategy.

Better accuracy and compliance. When pricing rules, discount limits, and configuration constraints are embedded in the assistant's reasoning, errors are caught before they reach the customer — not after an internal audit.

Higher deal size through guided selling. Real-time upsell and cross-sell recommendations aren't an afterthought; they're built into the quoting flow. Reps are prompted with relevant options at exactly the right moment.

Tighter SAP ecosystem integration. The Quoting Assistant works natively within SAP CPQ and SAP S/4HANA, which means no data re-entry, clean-core alignment, and full traceability across the quote lifecycle. Source

The Architecture Behind It: Assistants + Agents

The Quoting Assistant doesn't work alone. It's part of SAP's layered AI architecture: Joule Assistants — role-aligned, context-aware AI systems — sit above Joule Agents, which are the task specialists that execute individual steps. Source

You tell the Quoting Assistant what you want to accomplish in plain language. It interprets your intent, pulls in your business context (your CPQ rules, your pricing policies, your customer history), and coordinates the agents doing the actual work. You stay in control; the heavy lifting happens automatically.

This architecture is important because it means the Quoting Assistant isn't a standalone tool — it's part of SAP's Autonomous Enterprise vision, where AI handles routine execution so people can focus on decisions that require judgment.

A Real-World Scenario

Imagine a key account manager receives an email from a customer requesting a customised bundle of hardware and professional services across three countries, with specific delivery windows and a tight margin requirement.

Historically, this would take hours — coordinating with product management, pricing, and legal before a quote could even be drafted.

With the Joule Quoting Assistant, the rep pastes (or forwards) the customer email, and the assistant:

  1. Parses the request and maps it to available products and service SKUs.
  2. Checks configuration rules and flags any incompatible options.
  3. Proposes a compliant price structure with margin guardrails.
  4. Recommends a maintenance bundle and a support tier upsell.
  5. Drafts the proposal document and a personalised cover email.

The rep reviews, adjusts, approves. What took half a day now takes minutes.

What This Signals for the Future of Sales

SAP's investment in the Quoting Assistant reflects a broader industry shift: the sales rep of the near future is a reviewer and relationship manager, not a data entry clerk. AI handles the structure; humans handle the nuance.

For organisations running SAP CPQ or SAP Sales Cloud v2, this isn't a distant roadmap item — it's available now, and it integrates with the systems you already have. The question isn't whether to evaluate it; it's how quickly you can get it into the hands of your team.

The SAP Joule Quoting Assistant is part of the SAP Joule Assistants portfolio. Learn more at sap.com/use-cases/joule-assistant/quoting-ai.

entry.title: SAP Service and Asset Manager 2511.3 Now Available – What's New?
entry.content:
Following the new quarterly release cadence introduced earlier this year—one major release followed by three minor releases per year—SAP Service and Asset Manager 2511.3 is now available. Minor releases under this new strategy focus on targeted refinements and enhancements that build on the capabilities delivered in the major release, providing a predictable and low-disruption upgrade experience for customers. To learn more about the release strategy, read SAP Service and Asset Manager: New Release Strategy Incoming.

Now, let's take a closer look at what's new in SAP Service and Asset Manager 2511.3.

This release brings meaningful improvements across maintenance execution, AI-assisted work completion, inspection data capture, usability configuration, and warehouse operations. Together, these updates help technicians, supervisors, maintenance teams, and warehouse clerks work more accurately, gain better real-time visibility, and benefit from more intelligent and flexible mobile workflows.

Technician Job Briefing Agent

Knowing what to expect before arriving at a job site makes a real difference—fewer surprises, faster execution, and better first-time fix rates. With the 2511.3 release, SAP Service and Asset Manager introduces the Technician Job Briefing Agent: an AI-powered capability that generates a personalized, conversational job briefing for technicians before or during field execution.

The agent assembles all the key context a technician needs in one place—work order details, asset history, open notifications, safety precautions, and relevant documentation—and presents it as a clear, natural language summary directly within the app. No need to navigate multiple screens or systems to piece together the full picture.

The business impact is tangible: faster job readiness, fewer on-site delays caused by missing information, an improved first-time fix rate, and safer maintenance execution through upfront visibility into safety risks and compliance guidance.

 

Partial Operation Completion Progress

Supervisors and planners often need to know how work is progressing without interrupting field teams. Until now, that typically meant a phone call or waiting for a full completion confirmation. With the 2511.3 release, technicians can capture partial operation progress—such as 25% or 75% complete—directly when confirming operations in SAP Service and Asset Manager.

This gives supervisors real-time visibility into work-in-progress status from the back office, without requiring direct communication with the field. The benefits are practical and immediate:

  • Better resource and schedule planning based on live progress data.
  • Earlier detection of potential delays before they escalate.
  • More accurate work-status reporting across maintenance operations.

Enhanced AI-Assisted Job Completion

SAP Service and Asset Manager has been steadily expanding its AI-assisted job completion capabilities, helping technicians record outcomes more efficiently and accurately. The 2511.3 release delivers two important enhancements in this area.

  • Defect Detail Capture Aligned to Notification Item Fields. AI-assisted job completion now captures defect details that align with notification item fields in SAP. When technicians describe completed work—whether through speech input or natural language—the AI interprets and maps defect information to the corresponding notification fields automatically. This reduces manual data entry, minimizes the risk of errors or missing information, and helps ensure that defect records are complete and consistent across the organization.

 

  • Full Audit Trail for AI-Assisted Recommendations. Every AI-assisted recommendation used during the job completion process is now tracked and logged. This means organizations have full transparency into which fields were generated by AI and which were entered manually by the technician—without requiring additional effort from either party. This audit trail directly supports compliance, quality review, and governance requirements. Whether for internal audits, customer SLA reporting, or regulatory compliance, organizations can now demonstrate a clear record of AI involvement in work execution data—out of the box.

Long Text Support for Inspection Checklist Characteristics

Inspectors working in the field often need to capture detailed observations—findings that go well beyond a simple pass/fail result or a numeric measurement. Previously, this required workarounds or documentation in separate systems, creating fragmented records and additional manual effort.

With the 2511.3 release, SAP Service and Asset Manager now supports long text input directly within inspection checklist characteristics. Inspectors can record full notes and detailed observations in a single place, alongside the rest of the inspection record. This richer data flows directly into SAP, enabling:

  • Better analysis of inspection findings over time.
  • Improved traceability for asset condition and maintenance history.
  • Stronger compliance and documentation quality—without extra steps.

Configurable Tab Layout on Home and Overview Screens

Different roles and workflows require different information upfront. With the 2511.3 release, administrators can now configure which tabs appear—and in what order—on the Home and Overview screens in SAP Service and Asset Manager.

This means field workers see the most relevant information the moment they open the app, tailored to their role and day-to-day tasks. The benefits are straightforward:

  • Fewer clicks and less navigation time to reach the right information.
  • A more focused and role-appropriate user experience.
  • Improved adoption and daily efficiency across all user groups—technicians, inspectors, supervisors, and warehouse clerks alike.

Administrators manage this configuration without requiring development effort, making it easy to adjust as roles or processes evolve.

WalkMe-Guided Walkthroughs Now Available on Android

The 2511.2 release introduced WalkMe SDK support for customer-created in-app guided walkthroughs on iOS, allowing organizations to build contextual, step-by-step guidance tailored to their configured processes. With the 2511.3 release, this capability is now extended to Android devices, completing cross-platform coverage.

Administrators can configure and deploy custom walkthroughs for specific workflows and use cases, and these are surfaced directly inside the app as users navigate through their tasks. New users benefit from contextual help without ever leaving SAP Service and Asset Manager—reducing onboarding time and training costs, regardless of the device they use.

This is especially valuable for organizations with a mixed-device workforce or those rolling out the app to new teams, as it enables consistent, self-service onboarding at scale.

 

Ad-Hoc Bin-to-Bin Transfers for Warehouse Clerks

Inventory movement in a warehouse doesn't always follow a pre-planned process. Unexpected needs arise—a part is in the wrong location, a technician needs materials moved quickly, or stock needs to be reorganized on the spot. With the 2511.3 release, warehouse clerks can now perform ad-hoc bin-to-bin transfers directly within SAP Service and Asset Manager, without any prior planning required.

The process is simple and fast:

  • Clerks select the warehouse process type, then scan or manually enter the source and destination bins.
  • Both product-based and handling unit (HU) transfers are supported.
  • Transfers can optionally be confirmed immediately at task creation—with no quantity entry required for HU transfers.

This capability reduces inventory delays and improves part availability for maintenance and service teams—helping ensure the right materials are in the right place when they're needed, without adding administrative overhead.

 

Summary

The 2511.3 release of SAP Service and Asset Manager delivers a focused set of enhancements that meaningfully improve how technicians, supervisors, inspectors, and warehouse clerks work in the field. From real-time progress visibility, richer AI-assisted job completion, and the new Technician Job Briefing Agent, to long text inspection support, flexible screen configuration, cross-platform walkthroughs, and expanded warehouse capabilities—these updates continue to build a more intelligent, efficient, and connected mobile experience.

To learn more about SAP Service and Asset Manager and these new capabilities, visit the SAP Help Portal or explore the SAP Community for additional resources, blog posts, and Q&A.

entry.title: SAP Dynamic Forms 2606 Now Available – What's New?
entry.content:
The 2606 release of SAP Dynamic Forms brings meaningful advances across AI-driven automation, offline field capabilities, geographic availability, form governance, and deeper integration with SAP maintenance processes. From migrating legacy PDF forms automatically to expanding the platform to new Google Cloud Platform regions, this release helps organizations modernize faster and work more flexibly — wherever their teams operate.

Key highlights include AI-assisted form migration, fully offline support for form images and attachments, new GCP data center regions, a Form Builder view mode, a new timestamp control, enhanced notifications from form data, mass assignment of form definitions, and additional usability improvements.

AI-Assisted Form Migration

One of the most impactful enhancements in 2606 is AI-assisted form migration, which enables organizations to convert existing PDF forms into SAP Dynamic Forms definitions automatically — eliminating the need for manual recreation and significantly reducing setup time.

Using generative AI, the capability interprets the structure and content of an existing PDF form and generates the corresponding SAP Dynamic Forms definition, including fields, controls, sections, and grids, as well as key metadata. Users can then review, refine, and deploy the migrated form with minimal effort.

This dramatically lowers the barrier to adoption for organizations with large catalogs of paper or PDF-based forms, helping them modernize their processes faster and with less manual overhead.

Offline Support for Form Images and Attachments

Field workers frequently capture photos and attach files while completing forms in locations with limited or no connectivity. With the 2606 release, form instances downloaded to SAP Service and Asset Manager (SSAM) devices now also download all previously attached files and images — making the full form experience, including attachments, available offline.

All attachments can be opened directly on the device in the offline client. This release also adds support for SSAM's 'supervisor mode,' ensuring that reassigned forms can be reviewed with their attachments intact — even without a connection.

This enhancement is essential for organizations in industries such as utilities, manufacturing, and oil and gas, where technicians and inspectors frequently work in remote or connectivity-challenged environments.

 

Google Cloud Platform Data Center Expansion

The 2606 release extends the geographic availability of SAP Dynamic Forms with support for Google Cloud Platform (GCP) data centers, enabling customers in additional regions to deploy the solution closer to their operations. The following data centers are now supported:

  • cf-ap30 – Australia (Sydney)
  • cf-br30 – Brazil (São Paulo)
  • cf-eu30 – Europe (Frankfurt)
  • cf-jp30 – Japan (Osaka)
  • cf-sa30 – KSA (Dammam)
  • cf-sa31 – KSA (Dammam)
  • cf-us30 – US Central (IA)
  • cf-us31 – US Central (IA)*
  • cf-ap31 – Singapore**
  • cf-eu31 – Europe (Netherlands)**

Note: *cf-us31 is planned for SAP Dynamic Forms 2609. **cf-ap31 and cf-eu31 are planned for SAP Dynamic Forms 2612.

 

Form Builder View Mode (Read-Only Permissions)

The 2606 release introduces a view mode in Form Builder, adding support for read-only permissions on form definitions. This allows organizations to grant users visibility into form designs without enabling them to make changes — supporting review, audit, and governance scenarios where access control over form authoring is important.

New Timestamp Control with Time Zone Support

SAP Dynamic Forms 2606 introduces a new timestamp control that supports both device and browser time zones. This ensures that date and time values captured in forms are accurately recorded relative to the local context of the user completing the form — whether they are working on a mobile device in the field or using a browser in the office. This is particularly valuable for organizations operating across multiple time zones or geographies.

 

 

Enhanced Support for Creating Notifications from Forms

SAP Dynamic Forms 2606 expands the capability to create maintenance notifications directly from form data, reducing duplicate data entry and accelerating defect and issue reporting. This release adds support for three additional data types:

  • Long Text: Long text fields from forms can now be mapped to the notification long text, enabling richer defect descriptions to flow directly into SAP maintenance records.
  • GPS Point → GEF: GPS coordinates captured in forms can be transferred to the Geographic Enhancement Framework (GEF), supporting location-based maintenance and asset tracking.
  • Form Attachments → DMS: Attachments included in a form can be transferred to the Document Management System (DMS) as part of the notification creation process, keeping supporting evidence linked to the maintenance record.

Mass Assignment of Form Definitions to Task List Headers and Operations

The 2606 release introduces the ability to mass-assign form definitions to task list headers and operations, making it significantly easier to roll out forms at scale. Rather than assigning forms individually, administrators can now apply form definitions across multiple task list items in a single action, reducing administrative effort and accelerating deployment for organizations with large or complex maintenance task structures.

Additional Enhancements

The 2606 release also includes the following usability improvements:

  • Multi-Column Sorting: Sorting across multiple columns is now supported in Form Builder, Form Runner, and Administrator details lists, improving navigation and data management for users working with large volumes of form data.
  • Form Runner Status Display: Form status is now more prominently visible in Form Runner, helping users quickly understand the state of their forms at a glance.

Summary

The 2606 release of SAP Dynamic Forms brings together advances in AI automation, offline field capabilities, platform availability, and maintenance integration. These enhancements help organizations deploy forms faster, support field teams more effectively, and connect form-based workflows more tightly with their core SAP maintenance processes.
